The page stays yours. DyNote only adds a lightweight layer when you ask it to.

Local by design

Your notes stay with your browser.

DyNote has no login and no cloud notebook. Its content script processes the current page locally to place and restore the note you asked for.

  • Saved in chrome.storage.local on your device
  • No extension fetch, XHR, WebSocket, analytics, or account
  • JSON export and validated import stay on your device

Good to know

A clear margin of error.

DyNote is useful on ordinary pages and honest about the browser surfaces it cannot reach.

Does DyNote sync between devices?

No. Notes stay in the current browser profile. Use the local JSON backup when you need to carry them yourself.

Which pages can use it?

DyNote targets ordinary top-level HTTP and HTTPS pages. Browser-internal pages, extension stores, embedded frames, and closed shadow roots are outside its reach.

What happens when an import meets a note?

Existing notes stay unchanged. A differing ID collision is restored as a copy, an equivalent copy is skipped on repeat import, and each file is validated before merging.

Can a layout change move a note?

It can. DyNote uses contextual anchors and a saved position, but virtualized content, heavy redesigns, and responsive changes can make a best-effort match unavailable.

Browser limits: the overlay is part of the webpage DOM through a Shadow Root. A page may still inspect or style parts of its own browser environment, and DyNote does not promise encryption.
